ogTitle: Roi Et Temple Trip: How to Plan 2 Days of Merit-Making
ogDesc: From the Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol on its hilltop down to Luang Pho Yai and the in-town temples — paced so you're not worn out.
h1:
Roi Et Temple Trip
2 Days of Merit-Making
intro: Roi Et is a genuinely relaxing place to go temple-hopping, because it has both a big headline sight — the Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol, set on a hilltop in Nong Phok district — and a cluster of in-town temples you can visit one after another at an easy pace. The only catch is that the Chai Mongkol chedi sits a fair distance from the city, so if you plan it badly you'll wear yourself out and run out of time for the other temples. That's why we've laid it out as a 2-day plan: day one you head up the hill to the Chai Mongkol chedi, and day two you loop around Luang Pho Yai and the older temples in town without rushing.

blocks.html: Before the day-by-day details, here's the big picture. Roi Et's main merit-making temples fall into two clear zones. The first is Wat Pha Nam Thip Thep Prasit Wararam in Nong Phok district, home to the Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol, around 60–80 km from the city — about an hour to an hour and a half by car. The other zone is the temples within the municipal area: Wat Burapha Phiram, Wat Klang Ming Mueang, and Wat Sa Thong, all close together and just a few minutes apart on foot or by car. Because the distances are so different, we don't recommend cramming every temple into one day.

A lot of people who come to Roi Et for a single day try to do the Chai Mongkol chedi in the morning and rush back to the in-town temples in the afternoon. They end up driving all day until they're exhausted, with no time to actually sit and take in the atmosphere up on the hill. The final stretch of road up the hill is fairly winding, so you can't drive fast. If you can stay a night in Roi Et and split it across two days, it's far more comfortable and you get the full view from the chedi.

blocks.title: Getting-around tip
blocks.html: The Chai Mongkol chedi is far out and public transport isn't convenient. If you don't have your own car, it's better to hire a car with a driver or charter a vehicle for the round trip from town — that works out better value than a taxi by the trip, and a local driver knows the hill road well.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Up the hill — Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol, Nong Phok

items.activity: Breakfast in town, then set off
items.note: Fill the tank before leaving the city — fuel stations thin out around Nong Phok. Allow about an hour to an hour and a half of driving.

items.activity: Arrive at Wat Pha Nam Thip, start the climb up the chedi
items.note: The chedi is 101 m on each side — width, length, and height — over 6 levels, topped with a golden tiered umbrella. You go up one level at a time; the climb is a little tiring but worth it.

items.activity: Reach the top level, take in the view and pay respects to the Buddha relics
items.note: The top level is a viewpoint over the surrounding forest and hills. On a clear morning you can see far, and the air up here is cooler than down below.

items.activity: Find lunch around Nong Phok or along the way back
items.note: Shops in Nong Phok town have made-to-order dishes and som tam at a basic level. Don't expect anything fancy, but you'll eat well enough.

items.activity: Stop at Pha Mok Miwai / Pha Nam Yoi viewpoint (if you're still up for it)
items.note: It's in the same zone as the temple — a cliff overlooking the forest, good for photos before heading down. If you're already tired, skip it; no need to push.

items.activity: Drive back into Roi Et town, check in, rest
items.note: You'll get back to the city in the late afternoon. Save your energy for the next day's in-town temples.

blocks.text: What's special about Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol

blocks.html: This chedi sits on a hilltop within Wat Pha Nam Thip Thep Prasit Wararam. Its architecture blends Phra Pathom Chedi with Phra That Phanom — white and gold set against the sky and surrounding forest, which looks striking from below. It measures 101 m on every side, equal in width, length, and height, and was built on a 101-rai plot, echoing the city's name (Roi Et means "one hundred and one"). Each level inside has Buddha images and murals to walk through, while the top level enshrines the Buddha relics and is the best viewpoint.

items: Location — Pha Nam Yoi sub-district, Nong Phok district, around 60–80 km from the city, 1–1.5 hr by car.
Entry fee — Free; donations as you wish, with collection boxes to support the temple.
Dress code — It's a temple and a sacred site, so dress modestly with shoulders and knees covered.
Best time — Clear mornings give long views; in the cool season the air on the hill is especially pleasant.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Looping the in-town temples — Luang Pho Yai, Wat Klang Ming Mueang, Wat Sa Thong

items.activity: Start at Wat Burapha Phiram, pay respects to Luang Pho Yai
items.note: Phra Phuttha Rattana Mongkol Maha Muni is a standing Buddha in the blessing pose, around 59 m tall (67 m including the base), visible from far off. It's on Phadung Phanit Road in town.

items.activity: Drive or walk on to Wat Klang Ming Mueang
items.note: An old temple in the city center that enshrines Phra Phuttha Ming Mueang Mongkol, Roi Et's city Buddha. The grounds are shady and calm.

items.activity: Head to Wat Sa Thong to pay respects to Luang Pho Phra Sangkajai
items.note: A revered city Buddha for Roi Et locals — the plump, smiling figure people pray to for fortune and trade. It's on Hai Sok Road in town.

items.activity: Rest at Bueng Phlan Chai in the city center
items.note: A lake in the heart of Roi Et with a central island and a shrine. A nice place for a stroll to rest your legs before lunch.

items.activity: Lunch in town, try proper Isan food
items.note: Shops for som tam, larb, koi, and khao jee are easy to find in town. Cap off the merit-making trip with a tasty local meal.

items.name: Wat Burapha Phiram
items.blurb: Home to Luang Pho Yai, the tall standing Buddha in the blessing pose that's a Roi Et landmark. You can see it from far off and walk up to pay respects at the base.

items.name: Wat Klang Ming Mueang
items.blurb: An old temple in the city center enshrining Phra Phuttha Ming Mueang Mongkol, the city Buddha. Lovely, shady Isan architecture.

items.name: Wat Sa Thong
items.blurb: Home to Luang Pho Phra Sangkajai, a revered city Buddha people pray to for fortune and good trade. It's in town, an easy continuation from the other temples.

items: Dress modestly — Every temple is a sacred site: sleeved tops, knee-covering trousers or skirts, and shoes off where required.
Bring flowers, incense, and candles — There are offering stalls in front of the main temples at reasonable prices; give as much as you can.
Pack water and an umbrella — Especially at the Chai Mongkol chedi, where you walk in the open sun, and the Isan sun is strong at midday.
Allow time for the hill road — The last stretch before Wat Pha Nam Thip is winding and uphill; drive slowly and watch for oncoming traffic.

blocks.title: Can you do it in a single day?
blocks.html: If you really only have one day, you'll have to choose. If you want the Chai Mongkol chedi, give the whole day to Nong Phok and skip the in-town temples. If time is short and you'd rather not drive far, you can comfortably loop all three in-town temples in half a day. But to make coming all the way to Roi Et worthwhile, we'd nudge you to stay a night and do both days in full.

faq.q: How far is Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol from Roi Et town?
faq.a: It's at Wat Pha Nam Thip Thep Prasit Wararam in Pha Nam Yoi sub-district, Nong Phok district, around 60–80 km from the city — roughly 1 to 1.5 hours by car. The final stretch is a winding hill road, so allow extra time.

faq.q: How many days do you need to cover Roi Et's main temples?
faq.a: If you want both the Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol at Nong Phok and the in-town temples, 2 days is the way to go: day one up the hill to the chedi, day two looping the in-town temples. With only one day, you'll have to pick one or the other.

faq.q: Is there an entry fee for Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol?
faq.a: No entry fee — donations are as you wish, with collection boxes to support the temple. Dress modestly with shoulders and knees covered, as it's a sacred site.

faq.q: Which temple is Luang Pho Yai in Roi Et?
faq.a: It's at Wat Burapha Phiram on Phadung Phanit Road in the municipal area of Roi Et. It's a standing Buddha in the blessing pose named Phra Phuttha Rattana Mongkol Maha Muni, around 59 m tall (about 67 m including the base) and visible from far off.

faq.q: Can you visit Roi Et's temples without your own car?
faq.a: For the in-town temples you can walk or charter a tuk-tuk or taxi to loop around, but public transport to the Chai Mongkol chedi at Nong Phok isn't convenient. It's better to hire a car with a driver or charter a vehicle for the round trip from town — better value and safer.
